subject: Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@edgefin.com>, Sam Lopez <s.lopez@edgefin.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & next steps (post-demo)

Hi Priya / Sam -

Great to meet earlier - thanks for walking us through the EdgeFin use case. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we can plan a focused benchmark:

Key SLOs you mentioned:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation <= 120 ms for short responses (~50-200 tokens), p95 <= 300 ms for longer streams (up to 1k tokens).
- Throughput: baseline target ~300-400 requests/sec for primary trading flow; able to burst to ~1k/sec during peak market events.
- Concurrency: expected steady-state concurrency ~60-100 simultaneous sessions.
- Streaming: chunked streaming required for user-facing UX; inter-chunk latency < 200 ms (so UI updates feel immediate).
- Model quality: must match current baseline answers on our internal eval (~>94% semantic match on the curated prompt set).

What we need from you to run a representative benchmark:
1) Confirm the most common prompt templates (I attached edgefin_prompt_set_v1.json I pulled from the call notes).
2) Provide a realistic request mix (ratio of short/medium/long, % streaming vs non-streaming) - one-line table is fine.
3) Any security or network constraints for a test harness (e.g., traffic must originate from specific IP ranges).

Proposed Redwood next steps:
- Rishi/Dylan: draft benchmark harness + measurement definitions (latency buckets, token accounting, warm vs cold start, KV-cache priming).
- Run reproducible benchmark against candidate models and quant levels; provide report with reproducibility instructions.
- Share scripts + results and propose a 1-hour walkthrough.

Can you confirm the request mix and any must-have test constraints by EOD Wed PST? If yes, we'll schedule the run for Thurs/Fri.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.json

Thanks Marissa - this looks great and matches our internal notes. A few clarifications that will help make the benchmark representative:

Request mix (approx):
- 55% short queries (20-80 tokens) - primarily validation checks (non-streaming).
- 30% medium (80-300 tokens) - mostly streaming responses (progressive summary).
- 15% long (300-1,000 tokens) - full-session transcripts (streaming).

Burst profile: typical baseline 350 rps, can spike to 1,100 rps for ~2-5 mins during market opens.

Security/network: test traffic can come from Redwood test IP ranges; we'll whitelist in our firewall. No additional constraints.

We'll attach a slightly-expanded prompt set (see attached) with anonymized examples. Also adding our primary success criteria: p95 latency targets as you recapped; plus <0.5% error rate on tokenization/runtime failures.

Happy to have Redwood run the benchmark Thurs afternoon PST. Sam and I are available for the 1-hour walkthrough on Fri 10am PST.

- Priya
Director, Platform Engineering
EdgeFin, Inc.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & next steps (post-demo) - benchmark plan draft

Hi Marissa / Dylan -

Draft plan below. I'll put the spec into edgefin_benchmark_harness_spec.md (attached) and push the harness to the sandbox repo. Quick highlights:

Harness & tooling
- Traffic generator: modified vegeta-based tool that supports streaming chunk simulation and token-aware pacing (open-source fork internal to Redwood).
- Workload driver: configurable mixes (short/medium/long), burst profiles, and concurrency knobs.
- Measurement collector: per-request traces (start/end timestamps), per-chunk timestamps for streamed responses, token counts, and error codes.

Measurement definitions
- Generation latency (non-streaming): time from request received at front proxy to final token emitted (ms).
- Streaming chunk latency: time from request received to first chunk, and inter-chunk gap (ms). We'll report p50/p90/p95 for both first-chunk and inter-chunk gaps.
- Throughput: sustained successful requests/sec and tokens/sec over 1m/5m windows.
- Concurrency: active sessions measured as concurrent open streaming connections.
- Warm vs cold: warm = after 5min steady-state traffic or after KV-cache priming routine; cold = fresh instance (measure 1-3 cold starts during test).
- Reproducibility: capture exact harness config (seeded RNG), model binary/config, quantization level, exact prompt set file, and system metrics (GPU utilization, memory, host CPU).

Data artifacts we'll deliver
- Raw logs (per-request JSON lines), aggregated stats (latency buckets), and reproducibility README with commands to re-run.
- One-page executive summary with pass/fail vs EdgeFin targets.

Proposed timeline
- Wed: finalize harness spec + share reproducibility checklist.
- Thurs (PST afternoon): run full benchmark (they gave us green light).
- Fri 10am PST: 1-hour walkthrough with EdgeFin to review results and next steps.

Attachments: edgefin_benchmark_harness_spec.md, edgefin_slo_targets.xlsx

Let me know if we should expand what we capture (e.g., network-level packet timings) - otherwise I'll finalize spec today.

- Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
